questions.heading: The Four Scientific Questions
questions.subheading: Every investigation answers these four core inquiries with mathematical certainty:

q1.title: WHAT IS CHANGING?
q1.desc: Identify physical, hydrological, and biological indicators across Land Surface Temperature, Rainfall, Vegetation Greenness, and Terrestrial Water Storage.

q2.title: WHERE IS IT CHANGING?
q2.desc: Demarcate authentic geographic boundaries down to district-level administrative polygons with exact georeferenced coordinates.

q3.title: HOW MUCH IS IT CHANGING?
q3.desc: Compute quantitative rates of change per year and decade using robust Theil-Sen non-parametric median slopes and 95% confidence intervals.

q4.title: IS IT STATISTICALLY SIGNIFICANT?
q4.desc: Evaluate the null hypothesis of no trend using the rank-based Mann-Kendall test, calculating standardized Z-scores and exact two-tailed p-values.

lst.name: Land Surface Temperature (LST)
lst.desc: Daytime radiometric surface temperature from MODIS Terra thermal infrared bands.

rainfall.name: Monthly Precipitation
rainfall.desc: Calibrated multi-satellite microwave and radar precipitation from NASA GPM IMERG.

ndvi.name: Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI)
ndvi.desc: Surface canopy photosynthetic vitality derived from red and near-infrared reflectance.

tws.name: Terrestrial Water Storage Anomaly
tws.desc: Integrated groundwater, soil moisture, and surface water anomalies from satellite gravimetry.

solar.name: Surface Solar Irradiance
solar.desc: All-sky surface downward solar radiation flux from NASA POWER assimilations.

stats.tsiDisclaimer: This indicator summarizes the strength and consistency of observed environmental change in the selected data. It is not a probability or forecast of harm.
stats.insufficientData: Insufficient observations for a statistically reliable trend estimate.
